s.t: Wendy, John, and Michael lived in a tall house in a big city.
s.fr: Wendy, John, et Michael vivaient dans une grande maison dans une grande ville.

s.t: Their room was called the nursery.
s.fr: Leur chambre s’appelait la nursery.

s.t: Every night, the mother came to the nursery and told the children a story.
s.fr: Chaque nuit, la mère venait à la nursery et racontait une histoire aux enfants.

s.t: The best stories were about Peter Pan.
s.fr: Les meilleures histoires parlaient de Peter Pan.

s.t: "Peter Pan is a boy who never grows up," the mother said.
s.fr: « Peter Pan est un garçon qui ne grandit jamais, » dit la mère.

s.t: "His home is an island called Neverland, far away over the sea."
s.fr: « Sa maison est une île appelée Neverland, très loin au-dessus de la mer. »

paras.summary: Wendy, John, and Michael live in a nursery in a tall city house, where their mother tells them stories every night, and the best stories are about Peter Pan, a boy who never grows up and lives on the island of Neverland.

s.t: Often, at story time, a boy came and sat outside the nursery window.
s.fr: Souvent, à l’heure des histoires, un garçon venait et s’asseyait dehors devant la fenêtre de la nursery.

s.t: He listened at the window, for he had no mother to tell him stories.
s.fr: Il écoutait à la fenêtre, car il n’avait pas de mère pour lui raconter des histoires.

s.t: One night, the mother saw the boy at the window.
s.fr: Une nuit, la mère vit le garçon à la fenêtre.

s.t: She ran to him, and the boy flew out into the night.
s.fr: Elle courut vers lui, et le garçon s’envola dans la nuit.

paras.summary: A boy comes and sits outside the nursery window at story time, because he has no mother to tell him stories; one night the mother sees him, and he flies out into the night.

s.t: The mother closed the window fast.
s.fr: La mère ferma vite la fenêtre.

s.t: The boy was fast, but his shadow was not.
s.fr: Le garçon était rapide, mais son ombre ne l’était pas.

s.t: The window caught the shadow, and the shadow came off him.
s.fr: La fenêtre attrapa l’ombre, et l’ombre se détacha de lui.

paras.summary: The mother closes the window fast, and the window catches the shadow of the boy, who is not fast enough, and pulls it off him; the boy is gone, but his shadow is still in the nursery.

s.t: The mother took the shadow up from the floor.
s.fr: La mère ramassa l’ombre sur le sol.

s.t: She knew the boy would come back for it.
s.fr: Elle savait que le garçon reviendrait la chercher.

s.t: She rolled up the shadow and put it away in a drawer.
s.fr: Elle roula l’ombre et la rangea dans un tiroir.

paras.summary: The mother takes the shadow up from the floor and knows the boy will come back for it, so she rolls it up and puts it away in a drawer, where it stays without the children knowing anything about it.

s.t: One night, not long after, the nursery window was open.
s.fr: Une nuit, pas longtemps après, la fenêtre de la nursery était ouverte.

s.t: A little light flew in through the window.
s.fr: Une petite lumière entra en volant par la fenêtre.

s.t: The light was a fairy, and her name was Tinker Bell.
s.fr: La lumière était une fée, et son nom était Tinker Bell.

s.t: She flew around the dark room, and her light went with her.
s.fr: Elle vola autour de la pièce sombre, et sa lumière l’accompagna.

s.t: Peter Pan flew in after her.
s.fr: Peter Pan entra en volant après elle.

s.t: He had come back for his shadow.
s.fr: Il était revenu chercher son ombre.

paras.summary: One night the nursery window is open, and a little light flies in — the fairy Tinker Bell — with Peter Pan behind her, come back for his shadow while John and Michael sleep.

s.t: "Find my shadow, Tinker Bell," said Peter.
s.fr: « Trouve mon ombre, Tinker Bell, » dit Peter.

s.t: The fairy flew to the drawer, and her light fell on it.
s.fr: La fée vola vers le tiroir, et sa lumière tomba sur lui.

s.t: Peter opened the drawer, pulled his shadow out, and was glad to have it back.
s.fr: Peter ouvrit le tiroir, tira son ombre dehors, et fut content de l’avoir retrouvée.

s.t: He put the shadow at his feet, but it fell off.
s.fr: Il posa l’ombre à ses pieds, mais elle tomba.

s.t: He put soap on the shadow, but it fell to the floor again.
s.fr: Il mit du savon sur l’ombre, mais elle tomba de nouveau par terre.

s.t: Tinker Bell pulled at the shadow, but the shadow would not stick to Peter.
s.fr: Tinker Bell tira sur l’ombre, mais l’ombre ne voulait pas coller à Peter.

paras.summary: Tinker Bell finds the drawer, and Peter pulls his shadow out, but it will not stick to him, not with soap and not with the fairy's help, and it falls to the floor.

s.t: Peter sat down on the floor and cried.
s.fr: Peter s’assit par terre et pleura.

s.t: Wendy woke in her bed and saw the boy on the floor, with tears on his face.
s.fr: Wendy se réveilla dans son lit et vit le garçon par terre, avec des larmes sur son visage.

s.t: "Boy, why are you sad?" Wendy asked.
s.fr: « Garçon, pourquoi es-tu triste ? » demanda Wendy.

s.t: "My shadow will not stick to me," said the boy.
s.fr: « Mon ombre ne veut pas coller à moi, » dit le garçon.

s.t: "I am Peter Pan," he said.
s.fr: « Je suis Peter Pan, » dit-il.

s.t: "I am Wendy," she said.
s.fr: « Je suis Wendy, » dit-elle.

s.t: "I can sew your shadow on for you."
s.fr: « Je peux coudre ton ombre pour toi. »

paras.summary: Peter sits on the floor and cries, and Wendy wakes and sees the boy with tears on his face; she asks why he is sad, he says his shadow will not stick and names himself Peter Pan, and Wendy gives her own name and says she can sew the shadow on for him.

s.t: Wendy found a needle and thread, and Peter took the shadow up from the floor for her.
s.fr: Wendy trouva une aiguille et du fil, et Peter prit l’ombre du sol pour elle.

s.t: She sat down on her bed, and Peter sat still at her feet.
s.fr: Elle s’assit sur son lit, et Peter resta immobile à ses pieds.

s.t: Wendy sewed the shadow to Peter's feet with the needle and thread.
s.fr: Wendy cousit l’ombre aux pieds de Peter avec l’aiguille et le fil.

s.t: The needle went in and out, in and out of the shadow.
s.fr: L’aiguille allait et venait, entrant et sortant de l’ombre.

s.t: It hurt a little, but Peter did not pull his feet away.
s.fr: Cela faisait un peu mal, mais Peter ne retira pas ses pieds.

paras.summary: Wendy sits on her bed and sews the shadow to Peter's feet with a needle and thread, and though it hurts a little, Peter does not pull away.

s.t: When the shadow was on him, Peter jumped up from the floor.
s.fr: Quand l’ombre fut sur lui, Peter sauta du sol.

s.t: When Peter flew up, the shadow went up, and when he came down, it came down.
s.fr: Quand Peter monta en volant, l’ombre monta aussi, et quand il descendit, elle descendit aussi.

s.t: "See, Wendy, my shadow comes with me!" said Peter.
s.fr: « Regarde, Wendy, mon ombre vient avec moi ! » dit Peter.

paras.summary: With the shadow on, Peter jumps up and flies, and the shadow goes up and comes down with him, fast now, staying with him at last.

s.t: John and Michael woke in their beds and saw the boy over them.
s.fr: John et Michael se réveillèrent dans leurs lits et virent le garçon au-dessus d’eux.

s.t: "Who are you?" John asked.
s.fr: « Qui êtes-vous ? » demanda John.

s.t: "I am Peter Pan, and I come from Neverland," said Peter.
s.fr: « Je suis Peter Pan, et je viens de Neverland, » dit Peter.

s.t: "The lost boys are on the island with me, and I tell them the stories I hear at your window."
s.fr: « Les garçons perdus sont sur l’île avec moi, et je leur raconte les histoires que j’entends à votre fenêtre. »

s.t: "They fell from their beds when they were little, and no mother came for them."
s.fr: « Ils sont tombés de leurs lits quand ils étaient petits, et aucune mère n’est venue pour eux. »

paras.summary: John and Michael wake and see the boy over them, and Peter tells them he comes from Neverland, where the lost boys hear his stories — the very stories he listens to at the nursery window — because they fell from their beds when they were little and have no mother.

s.t: "Come with me, Wendy, and you can be our mother."
s.fr: « Viens avec moi, Wendy, et tu peux être notre mère. »

s.t: "You can tell us stories at night and sew for us."
s.fr: « Tu peux nous raconter des histoires la nuit et coudre pour nous. »

s.t: "I cannot leave John and Michael," said Wendy.
s.fr: « Je ne peux pas quitter John et Michael, » dit Wendy.

s.t: "They can come too," said Peter, and John and Michael got out of their beds fast to go with him.
s.fr: « Ils peuvent venir aussi, » dit Peter, et John et Michael sortirent vite de leurs lits pour aller avec lui.

s.t: "How can we go to Neverland?" John asked.
s.fr: « Comment pouvons-nous aller à Neverland ? » demanda John.

s.t: "We cannot fly like you," said Wendy.
s.fr: « Nous ne pouvons pas voler comme vous, » dit Wendy.

paras.summary: Peter asks Wendy to come and be the lost boys' mother; she cannot leave John and Michael, so Peter says they can come too, and the brothers jump out of bed fast, but John asks how they can go there when none of them can fly.

s.t: "You can fly too," said Peter to the children.
s.fr: « Vous pouvez voler aussi, » dit Peter aux enfants.

s.t: "I blow fairy dust on you, and you think of happy things."
s.fr: « Je souffle de la poussière de fée sur vous, et vous pensez à des choses heureuses. »

s.t: "The dust and the happy things take you up into the air, and you fly."
s.fr: « La poussière et les choses heureuses vous emportent dans l’air, et vous volez. »

s.t: Peter took Tinker Bell in his hand and blew her bright dust over the children and their beds.
s.fr: Peter prit Tinker Bell dans sa main et souffla sa poussière brillante sur les enfants et leurs lits.

s.t: Tinker Bell was angry when her dust fell on Wendy.
s.fr: Tinker Bell était en colère quand sa poussière tomba sur Wendy.

s.t: "Think of happy things now," said Peter, and the children closed their eyes to think.
s.fr: « Pensez à des choses heureuses maintenant, » dit Peter, et les enfants fermèrent leurs yeux pour penser.

paras.summary: Peter says the children can fly too: he blows Tinker Bell's fairy dust over them and tells them to think of happy things, which take them up into the air — though Tinker Bell is angry when her dust falls on Wendy.

s.t: Michael thought of his mother's stories, and his feet came up off the floor.
s.fr: Michael pensa aux histoires de sa mère, et ses pieds se levèrent du sol.

s.t: "I can fly!" Michael called.
s.fr: « Je peux voler ! » appela Michael.

s.t: He flew over the beds and did not know how to come down to the floor.
s.fr: Il vola au-dessus des lits et ne sut pas comment descendre jusqu’au sol.

s.t: John thought of pirates and pirate ships, and went up into the air after him.
s.fr: John pensa aux pirates et aux navires pirates, et monta dans l’air après lui.

s.t: Wendy thought of stories at night for the lost boys, and up she went too.
s.fr: Wendy pensa aux histoires du soir pour les garçons perdus, et elle monta aussi.

s.t: The children flew around the nursery with Peter, and their shadows flew with them on the floor.
s.fr: Les enfants volèrent autour de la nursery avec Peter, et leurs ombres volèrent avec eux sur le sol.

paras.summary: Michael thinks of his mother's stories and comes up off the floor, John thinks of pirates and pirate ships, Wendy thinks of telling stories to the lost boys, and soon the children are flying around the nursery with Peter, their shadows below them on the floor.

s.t: At the window, Peter took a button from his coat and put it in Wendy's hand.
s.fr: À la fenêtre, Peter prit un bouton de son manteau et le mit dans la main de Wendy.

s.t: Wendy put the button on a string and put the string around her neck.
s.fr: Wendy mit le bouton sur une ficelle et mit la ficelle autour de son cou.

s.t: "We go to Neverland now," said Peter.
s.fr: « Nous allons à Neverland maintenant, » dit Peter.

s.t: "How do we find Neverland?" John asked.
s.fr: « Comment trouvons-nous Neverland ? » demanda John.

s.t: "The second star to the right, and straight on till morning," said Peter.
s.fr: « La deuxième étoile à droite, et tout droit jusqu’au matin, » dit Peter.

s.t: Peter flew out through the window into the night, and Tinker Bell flew with him.
s.fr: Peter s’envola par la fenêtre dans la nuit, et Tinker Bell s’envola avec lui.

s.t: Wendy, John, and Michael flew out after him, over the city and up into the stars.
s.fr: Wendy, John, et Michael s’envolèrent après lui, au-dessus de la ville et jusque dans les étoiles.

paras.summary: At the window Peter puts a button in Wendy's hand, and she hangs it on a string around her neck; he names the way to Neverland — the second star to the right, and straight on till morning — and they all fly out over the city and up into the stars.

s.t: All night, Peter, Wendy, John, and Michael flew on over the dark sea, under the stars and the moon.
s.fr: Toute la nuit, Peter, Wendy, John, et Michael volèrent au-dessus de la mer sombre, sous les étoiles et la lune.

s.t: Michael was the littlest, and soon, over the dark sea, his eyes closed.
s.fr: Michael était le plus petit, et bientôt, au-dessus de la mer sombre, ses yeux se fermèrent.

s.t: He thought of nothing at all, and down he fell through the air toward the sea.
s.fr: Il ne pensa à rien du tout, et il tomba vers le bas à travers l’air en direction de la mer.

s.t: Wendy cried out, but Peter was fast and caught Michael by the arm.
s.fr: Wendy cria, mais Peter était rapide et attrapa Michael par le bras.

s.t: "Think of happy things again, Michael," said Peter.
s.fr: « Pense à des choses heureuses encore, Michael, » dit Peter.

s.t: Michael thought of the island, and up he went over the sea again.
s.fr: Michael pensa à l’île, et il monta au-dessus de la mer encore.

paras.summary: They fly all night over the dark sea, and when little Michael's eyes close and he thinks of nothing at all, he falls toward the water, but Peter is fast and catches him, and happy things take Michael up again.

s.t: Soon John's eyes closed too.
s.fr: Bientôt les yeux de John se fermèrent aussi.

s.t: Wendy saw and pulled him up by the arm.
s.fr: Wendy le vit et le tira vers le haut par le bras.

s.t: Tinker Bell flew down to Wendy and pulled her hair.
s.fr: Tinker Bell vola vers le bas jusqu’à Wendy et lui tira les cheveux.

s.t: "Tinker Bell is jealous of you," said Peter to Wendy.
s.fr: « Tinker Bell est jalouse de vous, » dit Peter à Wendy.

paras.summary: John's eyes close too, and Wendy pulls him up by the arm; Tinker Bell flies down and pulls Wendy's hair, and Peter says the fairy is jealous of her.

s.t: When morning came, the sun came up far over the sea.
s.fr: Quand le matin arriva, le soleil se leva loin au-dessus de la mer.

s.t: Far below them, down on the sea, they saw an island.
s.fr: Loin en dessous d’eux, sur la mer, ils virent une île.

s.t: "There is Neverland," said Peter.
s.fr: « Voilà Neverland, » dit Peter.

s.t: They came down out of the morning air and flew low over the island.
s.fr: Ils descendirent de l’air du matin et volèrent bas au-dessus de l’île.

paras.summary: They fly on toward the second star, straight on till morning, and when the sun comes up they see an island far below — Neverland — and they fly down low over it.

s.t: They saw the woods of the island, and a lagoon with mermaids in the water.
s.fr: Ils virent les bois de l’île, et un lagon avec des sirènes dans l’eau.

s.t: On the sea near the island, low in the water, they saw a ship.
s.fr: Sur la mer près de l’île, bas dans l’eau, ils virent un navire.

s.t: "A pirate ship!" John called out.
s.fr: « Un navire de pirates ! » cria John.

s.t: "The captain of that ship is called Hook," said Peter.
s.fr: « Le capitaine de ce navire s’appelle Hook, » dit Peter.

s.t: Tinker Bell flew down toward the woods first, fast, and Peter did not see her go.
s.fr: Tinker Bell vola vers le bas des bois en premier, vite, et Peter ne la vit pas partir.

paras.summary: They see the woods, a lagoon with mermaids in the water, and a ship near the island, whose captain Peter says is called Hook; Tinker Bell flies down toward the woods first, without Peter seeing her go.

s.t: In the air over the island, Tinker Bell came back to Wendy.
s.fr: Dans l’air au-dessus de l’île, Tinker Bell revint vers Wendy.

s.t: "Follow me down, and you will see the home of the lost boys first," said the fairy.
s.fr: « Suis-moi vers le bas, et tu verras la maison des garçons perdus en premier, » dit la fée.

s.t: Wendy followed her down toward the woods.
s.fr: Wendy la suivit vers le bas en direction des bois.

s.t: Tinker Bell flew fast, and soon Wendy was far back, alone in the air.
s.fr: Tinker Bell vola vite, et bientôt Wendy était loin derrière, seule dans l’air.

paras.summary: Over the island, Tinker Bell tells Wendy to follow her down for a first look at the lost boys' home, then flies so fast that Wendy is soon far back and alone in the air.

s.t: "A great white bird comes, and Peter says you must shoot it down!" Tinker Bell called to the lost boys.
s.fr: « Un grand oiseau blanc vient, et Peter dit que tu dois le tirer vers le bas ! » appela Tinker Bell les garçons perdus.

s.t: The boys believed her, for she was Peter's fairy.
s.fr: Les garçons la crurent, car elle était la fée de Peter.

s.t: One boy had a bow and a sharp arrow, and he looked up over the trees.
s.fr: Un garçon avait un arc et une flèche aiguisée, et il regarda vers le haut au-dessus des arbres.

s.t: A white thing flew over the trees toward them.
s.fr: Une chose blanche vola au-dessus des arbres vers eux.

s.t: "The Wendy bird!" called the boys, and the boy shot his arrow up at it.
s.fr: « L’oiseau Wendy ! » appelèrent les garçons, et le garçon tira sa flèche vers le haut sur lui.

paras.summary: Tinker Bell tells the lost boys that a great white bird is coming and that Peter says to shoot it down; the boys believe Peter's fairy, and when a white thing flies over the trees, one boy shoots his arrow at it.

s.t: The arrow hit, and Wendy fell down through the branches to the grass.
s.fr: La flèche toucha, et Wendy tomba vers le bas à travers les branches jusqu’à l’herbe.

s.t: The boys ran to her and saw a girl, not a bird.
s.fr: Les garçons coururent vers elle et virent une fille, pas un oiseau.

s.t: "She is dead," said one of the boys.
s.fr: « Elle est morte, » dit un des garçons.

s.t: Peter flew down through the trees with John and Michael.
s.fr: Peter descendit en volant à travers les arbres avec John et Michael.

s.t: "I brought you a mother, and you have shot her!" said Peter.
s.fr: « Je vous ai amené une mère, et vous l’avez tuée ! » dit Peter.

paras.summary: The arrow hits, and Wendy falls through the branches to the grass, where the boys find a girl, not a bird, and think her dead; Peter flies down with John and Michael and cries that they have shot the mother he brought them.

s.t: "Tinker Bell told us to shoot the bird," said the boy with the bow.
s.fr: « Tinker Bell nous a dit de tirer sur l’oiseau, » dit le garçon avec l’arc.

s.t: "I did not say that," said Peter, and he turned to the fairy.
s.fr: « Je n’ai pas dit cela, » dit Peter, et il se tourna vers la fée.

s.t: "Go away from me, Tinker Bell, and do not come back for many days."
s.fr: « Va-t’en de moi, Tinker Bell, et ne reviens pas pendant de nombreux jours. »

s.t: But Wendy was not dead.
s.fr: Mais Wendy n’était pas morte.

s.t: The arrow had hit the button on the string at her neck.
s.fr: La flèche avait frappé le bouton sur le cordon à son cou.

s.t: Wendy opened her eyes and saw the boys around her.
s.fr: Wendy ouvrit les yeux et vit les garçons autour d’elle.

paras.summary: The boy with the bow says Tinker Bell told them to shoot, and Peter, who said no such thing, sends the fairy away for many days; but Wendy is not dead — the arrow hit the button on the string at her neck — and she opens her eyes.

s.t: The lost boys went home under the ground, and Wendy, John, and Michael went with them.
s.fr: Les garçons perdus rentrèrent chez eux sous la terre, et Wendy, John et Michael partirent avec eux.

s.t: Every boy went down through his hollow tree, for the trees were the doors of the home.
s.fr: Chaque garçon descendit par son arbre creux, car les arbres étaient les portes de la maison.

s.t: One tree was wide, for one of the lost boys was big.
s.fr: Un arbre était large, car l’un des garçons perdus était grand.

s.t: Under the ground there was one warm room, with a bed for every one of the boys.
s.fr: Sous la terre il y avait une pièce chaude, avec un lit pour chacun des garçons.

paras.summary: The lost boys take the children to their home under the ground, where hollow trees are the doors and every boy goes down through his own tree — one tree wide because one boy is big — into one warm room with a bed for every boy.

s.t: Wendy was the mother of the home from that night on.
s.fr: Wendy fut la mère du foyer à partir de cette nuit-là.

s.t: She told the boys stories every night, as her mother had told her.
s.fr: Elle raconta aux garçons des histoires chaque nuit, comme sa mère lui en avait raconté.

s.t: She sewed their clothes with her needle and thread.
s.fr: Elle cousit leurs vêtements avec son aiguille et son fil.

s.t: Every night, she gave the boys their medicine from a little cup.
s.fr: Chaque nuit, elle donna aux garçons leur médicament dans une petite tasse.

s.t: The boys did not like the medicine, but they drank it, for Wendy was the mother.
s.fr: Les garçons n’aimaient pas le médicament, mais ils le burent, car Wendy était la mère.

paras.summary: Wendy becomes the mother of the home: she tells stories every night as her own mother did, sews the boys' clothes, and gives them medicine from a little cup, which they do not like but drink because she is the mother.

s.t: Peter was the father of the home, and the boys did as he said.
s.fr: Peter était le père du foyer, et les garçons faisaient comme il le disait.

s.t: All day, the children hunted and played in the woods with the lost boys.
s.fr: Toute la journée, les enfants chassèrent et jouèrent dans les bois avec les garçons perdus.

s.t: John and Michael forgot their old home a little more every day.
s.fr: John et Michael oublièrent un peu plus leur vieux foyer chaque jour.

s.t: But Wendy did not forget, and she told them of their mother and father.
s.fr: Mais Wendy n’oublia pas, et elle leur parla de leur mère et de leur père.

paras.summary: Peter is the father, the days pass in hunting and play in the woods, and John and Michael forget their old home a little more every day, though Wendy does not and tells them of their mother and father.

s.t: After many days, Tinker Bell came back to the home under the ground and said she was sorry.
s.fr: Après de nombreux jours, Tinker Bell revint au foyer sous la terre et dit qu’elle était désolée.

s.t: Peter was angry for days, but he let her come home.
s.fr: Peter fut en colère pendant des jours, mais il la laissa rentrer à la maison.

s.t: One night, after the medicine and the stories, Wendy asked Peter about fairies.
s.fr: Un soir, après la médecine et les histoires, Wendy demanda à Peter ce qu’il pensait des fées.

s.t: "A fairy light is strong when children believe in fairies," said Peter.
s.fr: « La lumière d’une fée est forte quand les enfants croient aux fées, » dit Peter.

s.t: "When children say they do not believe in fairies, a fairy light must go out."
s.fr: « Quand les enfants disent qu’ils ne croient pas aux fées, la lumière d’une fée doit s’éteindre. »

paras.summary: After many days Tinker Bell comes back sorry, and Peter lets her come home; one night Peter tells Wendy that a fairy light is strong when children believe in fairies, and that it must go out when children say they do not believe.

s.t: The pirate ship of Captain Hook was on the sea near the island.
s.fr: Le navire pirate du capitaine Hook était sur la mer près de l’île.

s.t: Hook, the captain of the pirates, had a long coat with gold buttons and long hair.
s.fr: Hook, le capitaine des pirates, portait un long manteau avec des boutons dorés et de longs cheveux.

s.t: His right hand was gone.
s.fr: Sa main droite avait disparu.

s.t: An iron hook was on his right arm now.
s.fr: Un crochet de fer était maintenant sur son bras droit.

s.t: That was why the pirates called him Hook.
s.fr: C’est pour cela que les pirates l’appelaient Hook.

paras.summary: On the pirate ship near the island is Hook, the captain of the pirates, who has a long coat with gold buttons, long hair, and an iron hook on his right arm where his right hand once was.

s.t: In a great fight one day, Peter Pan had cut off Hook's right hand.
s.fr: Un jour, lors d’un grand combat, Peter Pan avait coupé la main droite de Hook.

s.t: The hand fell into the sea, and a crocodile ate it.
s.fr: La main tomba dans la mer, et un crocodile la mangea.

s.t: From that day on, the crocodile followed Hook over the sea, for it wanted the rest of him.
s.fr: À partir de ce jour, le crocodile suivit Hook sur la mer, car il voulait le reste de lui.

paras.summary: Hook is afraid of one thing in the sea: long ago Peter Pan cut off his hand in a fight, and the crocodile that ate it has followed Hook ever since, wanting the rest of him.

s.t: One day, the crocodile ate a clock too.
s.fr: Un jour, le crocodile mangea aussi une horloge.

s.t: The clock was still inside it, and it still made its sound: tick, tick.
s.fr: L’horloge était encore à l’intérieur, et elle faisait encore son son : tic-tac, tic-tac.

s.t: When the crocodile came near the ship, the tick came first.
s.fr: Quand le crocodile s’approchait du navire, le tic-tac arrivait en premier.

s.t: When Hook heard the tick, he knew the crocodile was near, and he turned and ran.
s.fr: Quand Hook entendait le tic, il savait que le crocodile était proche, et il se retournait et courait.

paras.summary: The crocodile once ate a clock too, and the clock inside it still makes its sound — tick, tick — so the tick always comes first, and when Hook hears it, he turns and runs.

s.t: One night, on the ship, Hook talked to his pirates about Peter Pan and the fight.
s.fr: Une nuit, sur le navire, Hook parla à ses pirates de Peter Pan et du combat.

s.t: "It was Peter Pan who cut off my hand," Hook said to them that night.
s.fr: « C’était Peter Pan qui m’avait coupé la main, » leur dit Hook ce soir-là.

s.t: "One day I will find his home, and I will kill him with my iron hook."
s.fr: « Un jour je trouverai sa maison, et je le tuerai avec mon crochet de fer. »

s.t: From the dark water came a sound: tick, tick.
s.fr: De l’eau sombre vint un son : tic-tac, tic-tac.

s.t: The great crocodile swam near the ship, and its two green eyes were up over the dark water.
s.fr: Le grand crocodile nagea près du navire, et ses deux yeux verts étaient au-dessus de l’eau sombre.

s.t: Hook turned white at the sound and ran inside the ship.
s.fr: Hook devint blanc au son et courut à l’intérieur du navire.

paras.summary: One night Hook tells his pirates that Peter Pan cut off his hand and that one day he will find Peter's home and kill him with his iron hook; then a tick comes from the dark water, the crocodile swims near, and Hook turns white and runs inside, so the pirates see that their great captain is afraid.

s.t: One day, the children went down to the lagoon to see the mermaids in the water.
s.fr: Un jour, les enfants descendirent à le lagon pour voir les sirènes dans l’eau.

s.t: A great rock stood up out of the water in the lagoon.
s.fr: Un grand rocher s’élevait hors de l’eau dans le lagon.

s.t: When the sun went low, the mermaids swam down to their caves under the water.
s.fr: Quand le soleil descendit bas, les sirènes nagèrent jusqu’à leurs grottes sous l’eau.

s.t: The children sat on the great rock in the last light.
s.fr: Les enfants s’assirent sur le grand rocher dans la dernière lumière.

s.t: A boat came over the water from the pirate ship.
s.fr: Un bateau vint sur l’eau depuis le navire pirate.

s.t: Peter saw it first, and the children went down from the rock into the water to hide.
s.fr: Peter le vit en premier, et les enfants descendirent du rocher dans l’eau pour se cacher.

paras.summary: The children go to the lagoon to see the mermaids, and when the sun goes low and the mermaids swim down to their caves, the children sit on the great rock; a boat comes from the pirate ship, and the children slip down into the water to hide.

s.t: In the boat were two pirates, and with them was a girl.
s.fr: Dans le bateau se trouvaient deux pirates, et avec eux se trouvait une fille.

s.t: The girl was Tiger Lily, the princess of the island people.
s.fr: La fille était Tiger Lily, la princesse du peuple de l’île.

s.t: Her hands were tied with rope.
s.fr: Ses mains étaient liées avec de la corde.

s.t: She had gone too near the pirate ship in the night, and the pirates had caught her.
s.fr: Elle s’était approchée trop près du navire pirate dans la nuit, et les pirates l’avaient capturée.

s.t: The two pirates put Tiger Lily out on the wet rock.
s.fr: Les deux pirates posèrent Tiger Lily sur le rocher mouillé.

s.t: "The water will rise over the rock in the night," said one pirate.
s.fr: « L’eau montera sur le rocher dans la nuit, » dit un pirate.

s.t: "And the princess cannot swim with her hands tied," said the other pirate.
s.fr: « Et la princesse ne peut pas nager avec les mains liées, » dit l’autre pirate.

paras.summary: In the boat are two pirates with a girl — Tiger Lily, the princess of the island people — her hands tied with rope because she went too near the pirate ship; they put her on the rock, where the water will rise in the night and she cannot swim.

s.t: Behind the rock, Peter made his voice deep, like the voice of Hook.
s.fr: Derrière le rocher, Peter rendit sa voix grave, comme la voix de Hook.

s.t: "Set the princess free!" came the deep voice over the water.
s.fr: « Libérez la princesse ! » vint la voix grave sur l’eau.

s.t: The two pirates believed it was the voice of their captain, Hook.
s.fr: Les deux pirates crurent que c’était la voix de leur capitaine, Hook.

s.t: They were afraid, and they took the ropes off Tiger Lily.
s.fr: Ils avaient peur, et ils retirèrent les cordes de Tiger Lily.

s.t: Tiger Lily went down into the water without a sound, and she saw Peter behind the rock.
s.fr: Tiger Lily descendit dans l’eau sans un bruit, et elle vit Peter derrière le rocher.

s.t: She swam away home to her people, and Peter laughed low at his trick.
s.fr: Elle nagea jusqu’à chez les siens, et Peter rit doucement de sa ruse.

paras.summary: Behind the rock, Peter makes his voice deep like Hook's and calls out to set the princess free; the pirates believe it is their captain's voice and, afraid, take the ropes off her; Tiger Lily slips into the water, sees Peter behind the rock, and swims home to her people, while Peter laughs low at his trick.

s.t: But that night, Hook came out to the lagoon.
s.fr: Mais cette nuit-là, Hook sortit vers le lagon.

s.t: He swam out to the rock, and the two pirates took him up into the boat.
s.fr: Il nagea jusqu’au rocher, et les deux pirates le hissèrent dans la barque.

s.t: "We set the princess free, as you told us," said a pirate.
s.fr: « Nous avons libéré la princesse, comme vous nous l’avez dit, » dit un pirate.

s.t: "I did not tell you that," said Hook.
s.fr: « Je ne vous ai pas dit cela, » dit Hook.

s.t: "A voice came over the water, and it was your voice," said the other pirate.
s.fr: « Une voix vint sur l’eau, et c’était votre voix, » dit l’autre pirate.

paras.summary: That night Hook comes out to the lagoon, and the two pirates tell him they set the princess free as he told them to — but he told them nothing, and the voice they heard over the water was not his.

s.t: "Who is there?" Hook called out over the dark water of the lagoon.
s.fr: « Qui est là ? » Hook appela sur l’eau sombre du lagon.

s.t: "I am Peter Pan!" came the voice of a boy over the water.
s.fr: « Je suis Peter Pan ! » vint la voix d’un garçon sur l’eau.

s.t: "Take him!" Hook called to his pirates.
s.fr: « Prenez-le ! » Hook appela ses pirates.

s.t: Peter flew up over the rock with his dagger out.
s.fr: Peter s’envola au-dessus du rocher avec son poignard sorti.

s.t: Hook jumped from the boat to the rock, and his iron hook went at Peter through the air.
s.fr: Hook sauta du bateau sur le rocher, et son crochet de fer alla vers Peter dans l’air.

paras.summary: Hook calls out to ask who is there, and Peter cannot help calling back that he is Peter Pan; Hook sends his pirates at him and jumps to the rock, his iron hook cutting the air, as Peter flies up with his dagger out.

s.t: Peter and Hook fought on the rock, over the dark water.
s.fr: Peter et Hook se battirent sur le rocher, au-dessus de l’eau sombre.

s.t: Again and again the iron hook came down at Peter, and again and again Peter was not there.
s.fr: Encore et encore le crochet de fer descendit vers Peter, et encore et encore Peter n’était pas là.

s.t: From the dark water came the tick, tick of the clock, and Hook stood still.
s.fr: De l’eau sombre vint le tic-tac, tic-tac de l’horloge, et Hook resta immobile.

s.t: The crocodile came up out of the water with its jaws open.
s.fr: Le crocodile sortit de l’eau avec ses mâchoires ouvertes.

s.t: Hook jumped into the water and swam for his ship, and the crocodile swam after him.
s.fr: Hook sauta dans l’eau et nagea vers son navire, et le crocodile nagea après lui.

paras.summary: Peter and Hook fight on the rock over the dark water, the iron hook coming down again and again without touching Peter, until the tick, tick of the clock comes from the water and Hook stands still; the crocodile comes up with its jaws open, and Hook jumps in and swims for his ship with the crocodile after him.

s.t: The water had risen over the rock, and Peter took Wendy's hand, and they flew home over the water.
s.fr: L’eau avait monté au-dessus de la roche, et Peter prit la main de Wendy, et ils volèrent chez-eux au-dessus de l’eau.

s.t: Tiger Lily told her people that Peter had set her free at the rock.
s.fr: Tiger Lily dit à son peuple que Peter l’avait libérée à la roche.

s.t: After that night, the island people were friends of Peter and the lost boys.
s.fr: Après cette nuit, les gens de l’île étaient amis de Peter et des garçons perdus.

paras.summary: The pirates turn the boat and row away after their captain; the water has risen over the rock, and Peter takes Wendy's hand and they all fly home, and after Tiger Lily tells her people that Peter set her free, the island people are friends of Peter and the lost boys.

s.t: Far away, over the sea, the tall house stood in the big city.
s.fr: Loin, au-dessus de la mer, la grande maison se trouvait dans la grande ville.

s.t: In the nursery of the tall house, three beds stood empty, night after night.
s.fr: Dans la nursery de la grande maison, trois lits se trouvaient vides, nuit après nuit.

s.t: Every night, the mother opened the nursery window and kept watch.
s.fr: Chaque nuit, la mère ouvrait la fenêtre de la nursery et montait la garde.

s.t: "The window must be open when the children come home," she said to the father.
s.fr: « La fenêtre doit être ouverte quand les enfants rentrent à la maison, » dit-elle au père.

s.t: The father sat with her by the open window in the cold.
s.fr: Le père s’assit avec elle près de la fenêtre ouverte dans le froid.

s.t: Days went by, and then months went by, and still the window stood open, and still the mother waited.
s.fr: Les jours passèrent, et puis les mois passèrent, et la fenêtre restait toujours ouverte, et la mère attendait toujours.

paras.summary: Far away in the big city, the three beds in the nursery stand empty night after night, and every night the mother opens the window and waits with the father beside her, crying over the empty beds on many nights, as days and months go by.

s.t: But one day, Wendy asked John about the home over the sea.
s.fr: Mais un jour, Wendy demanda à John des nouvelles de la maison au-delà de la mer.

s.t: "John, do you remember our mother and our father?" she asked.
s.fr: « John, tu te souviens de notre mère et de notre père ? » demanda-t-elle.

s.t: John thought and thought.
s.fr: John réfléchit et réfléchit.

s.t: "I remember a little of the home," said John.
s.fr: « Je me souviens un peu de la maison, » dit John.

s.t: "I remember the stories, but I do not remember her face."
s.fr: « Je me souviens des histoires, mais je ne me souviens pas de son visage. »

paras.summary: In Neverland the children know nothing of the tears at home, but one day Wendy asks John about the home over the sea and whether he remembers their mother and father, and John remembers the stories but not their mother's face.

s.t: Wendy turned to Michael.
s.fr: Wendy se tourna vers Michael.

s.t: "Michael, do you remember our mother?"
s.fr: « Michael, tu te souviens de notre mère ? »

s.t: "You are my mother, Wendy," said Michael.
s.fr: « Tu es ma mère, Wendy, » dit Michael.

s.t: Wendy looked at him and had nothing to say.
s.fr: Wendy le regarda et n’avait rien à dire.

s.t: "Soon we must go home to our mother and father," said Wendy.
s.fr: « Bientôt nous devons rentrer chez notre mère et notre père, » dit Wendy.

s.t: John and Michael said yes, and then they ran out to play again.
s.fr: John et Michael dirent oui, et puis ils coururent dehors pour jouer encore.

paras.summary: When Wendy asks Michael, he says that Wendy is his mother, and she has nothing to say to that; she tells them they must soon go home, and the brothers say yes and then run out to play again.

s.t: That night, Wendy gave the boys the medicine from the cup, and then she told them a story.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, Wendy donna aux garçons le médicament de la tasse, et puis elle leur raconta une histoire.

s.t: "There was a mother who had three children," said Wendy to the boys.
s.fr: « Il y avait une mère qui avait trois enfants, » dit Wendy aux garçons.

s.t: "One night, the children flew away from her, out the window and far away over the sea."
s.fr: « Une nuit, les enfants s’envolèrent loin d’elle, par la fenêtre et bien loin au-dessus de la mer. »

s.t: "The mother waited for them, and the window was open every night, for she knew they would come home."
s.fr: « La mère les attendit, et la fenêtre était ouverte chaque nuit, car elle savait qu’ils rentreraient à la maison. »

paras.summary: That night, after the medicine, Wendy tells the boys a story: a mother whose three children flew away from her over the sea, and whose window is open every night because she knows they will come home.

s.t: "Did the three children go home to her?" said Michael.
s.fr: « Les trois enfants rentrèrent-ils chez elle ? » dit Michael.

s.t: "They flew home to her at last, and the mother was at the open window."
s.fr: « Ils rentrèrent chez elle à la fin, et la mère était à la fenêtre ouverte. »

s.t: "That mother is our mother, and we are the three children in the story," said Wendy.
s.fr: « Cette mère est notre mère, et nous sommes les trois enfants de l’histoire, » dit Wendy.

s.t: "We must go home to our mother tonight."
s.fr: « Nous devons rentrer chez notre mère ce soir. »

paras.summary: When Michael asks if the children went home, Wendy says they flew home at last and the mother was at the open window; then she tells them the story is their own story, and that they must go home tonight.

s.t: "I want to see our mother," said Michael, and John came up out of his bed.
s.fr: « Je veux voir notre mère, » dit Michael, et John se leva de son lit.

s.t: The lost boys did not want Wendy to go.
s.fr: Les garçons perdus ne voulaient pas que Wendy parte.

s.t: "Come with us, and our mother and father will take you in," she said.
s.fr: « Venez avec nous, et notre mère et notre père vous accueilleront, » dit-elle.

s.t: The lost boys said they would come to the home over the sea.
s.fr: Les garçons perdus dirent qu’ils viendraient dans la maison au-dessus de la mer.

s.t: But Peter said, "I will not go with you."
s.fr: Mais Peter dit, « Je ne partirai pas avec vous. »

s.t: "In that home, they will make me go to school and grow up, and I will never grow up."
s.fr: « Dans cette maison, ils me feront aller à l’école et grandir, et je ne grandirai jamais. »

paras.summary: Michael wants to see their mother, and Wendy asks the lost boys to come too, for her mother and father will take them in; the lost boys say yes, but Peter will not go, for in that home they would make him go to school and grow up.

s.t: Wendy filled Peter's cup with his medicine and put it on the shelf by the wide tree.
s.fr: Wendy remplit la tasse de Peter avec son médicament et la posa sur l’étagère près du grand arbre.

s.t: "Promise me you will drink your medicine every night after we go home," said Wendy.
s.fr: « Promets-moi que tu boiras ton médicament chaque soir après que nous rentrerons à la maison, » dit Wendy.

s.t: "I promise," said Peter, and he went to his bed.
s.fr: « Je promets, » dit Peter, et il alla à son lit.

s.t: After the fight at the lagoon, Hook had walked the dark woods every night to find Peter's home.
s.fr: Après le combat au lagon, Hook avait parcouru les bois sombres chaque nuit pour trouver la maison de Peter.

s.t: At last, he had seen one of the lost boys go down a hollow tree.
s.fr: Enfin, il avait vu un des garçons perdus descendre dans un arbre creux.

s.t: Now Hook and his pirates waited in the woods over the home of Peter and the boys.
s.fr: Maintenant, Hook et ses pirates attendaient dans les bois au-dessus de la maison de Peter et des garçons.

paras.summary: Wendy fills Peter's cup with medicine, puts it on the shelf by the wide tree, and makes him promise to drink it every night; meanwhile Hook, who has walked the woods every night since the fight at the lagoon and seen a lost boy go down a hollow tree, waits with his pirates over the home.

s.t: That night, the children went up out of the home under the ground, and Peter did not go with them.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, les enfants sortirent de la maison souterraine, et Peter ne sortit pas avec eux.

s.t: Wendy went up, and John and Michael and the lost boys came after her, one by one.
s.fr: Wendy monta, et John et Michael et les garçons perdus vinrent après elle, un par un.

s.t: But the pirates of Hook waited at the trees in the dark.
s.fr: Mais les pirates de Hook attendaient aux arbres dans l’obscurité.

s.t: As they came up, the pirates took them and put hands over their mouths.
s.fr: Quand ils sortirent, les pirates les prirent et mirent des mains sur leurs bouches.

paras.summary: That night the children go up out of the home one by one, without Peter, but Hook's pirates are waiting at the trees in the dark, and they take each one and put hands over their mouths.

s.t: No cry and no sound went down to Peter under the ground.
s.fr: Aucun cri et aucun son ne descendit jusqu’à Peter sous la terre.

s.t: The pirates tied the children and the lost boys with ropes, hand and foot.
s.fr: Les pirates attachèrent les enfants et les garçons perdus avec des cordes, pieds et mains.

s.t: They carried them through the dark woods, down to the black ship at anchor on the sea.
s.fr: Ils les portèrent à travers les bois sombres, jusqu’au navire noir à l’ancre sur la mer.

paras.summary: No sound goes down to Peter, and the pirates tie the children and the lost boys with ropes, hand and foot, and carry them through the dark woods to the black ship, while Peter sleeps on his bed and does not hear them go.

s.t: Hook did not go down to the ship with his pirates.
s.fr: Hook ne descendit pas au navire avec ses pirates.

s.t: The trees were too little for Hook, but the wide tree took him down.
s.fr: Les arbres étaient trop petits pour Hook, mais le grand arbre le fit descendre.

s.t: At the foot of the tree, the way in was low.
s.fr: Au pied de l’arbre, l’entrée était basse.

s.t: Hook could not get through the low way, but he could see the bed where Peter slept.
s.fr: Hook ne pouvait pas passer par l’entrée basse, mais il pouvait voir le lit où Peter dormait.

s.t: On the shelf by the foot of the tree was the cup of medicine.
s.fr: Sur l’étagère au pied de l’arbre se trouvait la tasse de médicament.

s.t: Hook carried a little bottle of poison with him that night.
s.fr: Hook porta une petite bouteille de poison avec lui cette nuit-là.

s.t: His arm went in through the low way, and the poison went into the cup, drop by drop.
s.fr: Son bras passa par l’entrée basse, et le poison tomba dans la tasse, goutte à goutte.

paras.summary: Hook stays behind, and the wide tree takes him down; the way in at the foot of the tree is too low for him, but he can see the bed where Peter sleeps, and the cup of medicine is on the shelf, so his arm goes in with the bottle of poison, and the poison goes into the cup, drop by drop.

s.t: Hook went up the wide tree and away into the dark woods.
s.fr: Hook remonta par le grand arbre et disparut dans les bois sombres.

s.t: As he walked, he talked to himself.
s.fr: Pendant qu’il marchait, il se parlait à lui-même.

s.t: "The children are on my ship, and there is poison in Pan's cup," said Hook.
s.fr: « Les enfants sont sur mon navire, et il y a du poison dans la coupe de Pan », dit Hook.

s.t: Tinker Bell was out in the woods that night, and she heard all that Hook said.
s.fr: Tinker Bell était dehors dans les bois ce soir-là, et elle entendit tout ce que Hook dit.

s.t: She flew down the wide tree to Peter.
s.fr: Elle descendit en volant le grand arbre jusqu’à Peter.

paras.summary: Hook goes up and away through the dark woods, talking to himself about the children on his ship and the poison in Pan's cup — and Tinker Bell, out in the woods that night, hears all that he says and flies down the wide tree to Peter.

s.t: Tinker Bell flew down into the quiet home and to Peter's bed.
s.fr: Tinker Bell descendit en volant dans la maison silencieuse et jusqu’au lit de Peter.

s.t: "Wake up, Peter!" she called, and Peter woke.
s.fr: « Réveille-toi, Peter ! » cria-t-elle, et Peter se réveilla.

s.t: "The pirates came in the night and took Wendy and the boys to the ship!"
s.fr: « Les pirates sont venus dans la nuit et ont emmené Wendy et les garçons au navire ! »

s.t: Peter got up fast from his bed and put his dagger in his belt.
s.fr: Peter se leva vite de son lit et mit son poignard dans sa ceinture.

s.t: "I will save them, but I must drink my medicine, for I promised Wendy."
s.fr: « Je vais les sauver, mais je dois boire ma médecine, car j’ai promis à Wendy. »

paras.summary: Tinker Bell flies down and wakes Peter with the news that the pirates have taken Wendy and the boys to the ship; he puts his dagger in his belt and says he will save them — but first his medicine, for he promised Wendy.

s.t: Peter took the cup down from the shelf.
s.fr: Peter prit la coupe en bas de l’étagère.

s.t: "Do not drink it, for Hook came down, and there is poison in your cup!"
s.fr: « Ne le bois pas, car Hook est descendu, et il y a du poison dans ta coupe ! »

s.t: "Hook cannot get down our trees," said Peter, and he did not believe her.
s.fr: « Hook ne peut pas descendre par nos arbres », dit Peter, et il ne la crut pas.

s.t: Peter put the cup to his mouth, but Tinker Bell flew in fast and drank the medicine down.
s.fr: Peter posa la tasse à sa bouche, mais Tinker Bell entra vite et but le médicament.

paras.summary: As Peter takes the cup from the shelf, Tinker Bell warns him that Hook was here and there is poison in it, but Peter does not believe Hook can get down the trees, so he lifts the cup — and Tinker Bell flies in fast and drinks all the medicine herself.

s.t: "That was my medicine!" said Peter.
s.fr: « C’était mon médicament ! » dit Peter.

s.t: But her light grew weak, and she fell down into Peter's hand.
s.fr: Mais sa lumière devint faible, et elle tomba dans la main de Peter.

s.t: "There was poison in it, Peter," she said, and her voice was slow.
s.fr: « Il y avait du poison dedans, Peter, » dit-elle, et sa voix était lente.

s.t: "You drank the poison to save me, and your light must not go out!" said Peter.
s.fr: « Tu as bu le poison pour me sauver, et ta lumière ne doit pas s’éteindre ! » dit Peter.

paras.summary: Her light grows weak and she falls into Peter's hand, telling him with a slow voice that there was poison in it; she drank it to save him, and Peter says her light must not go out.

s.t: He took her in his hands and flew up, high over the homes of the island people.
s.fr: Il la prit dans ses mains et s’envola, haut au-dessus des maisons des gens de l’île.

s.t: "I am Peter Pan, and I believe in fairies!" he called down in the night.
s.fr: « Je suis Peter Pan, et je crois aux fées ! » cria-t-il vers le bas dans la nuit.

s.t: The children of the island people woke and knew that name, for he set their princess free.
s.fr: Les enfants des gens de l’île se réveillèrent et connurent ce nom, car il avait libéré leur princesse.

s.t: "We believe in fairies too!" the children called back up to him from their homes.
s.fr: « Nous croyons aussi aux fées ! » crièrent les enfants vers lui depuis leurs maisons.

s.t: In Peter's hands, Tinker Bell's light grew strong again.
s.fr: Dans les mains de Peter, la lumière de Tinker Bell devint forte de nouveau.

s.t: She flew up, well again, and she and Peter flew fast to the ship.
s.fr: Elle s’envola, guérie de nouveau, et elle et Peter volèrent vite vers le navire.

paras.summary: Peter flies high over the homes of the island people, calling down that he is Peter Pan and believes in fairies, and the children, who know the name of the boy who set their princess free, call back that they believe too; Tinker Bell's light grows strong again, and she flies up well, and the two of them fly fast toward the ship.

s.t: On the deck of the pirate ship, the children were tied to the mast.
s.fr: Sur le pont du navire pirate, les enfants étaient attachés au mât.

s.t: Hook walked up and down the deck.
s.fr: Hook arpenta le pont.

s.t: "Join my crew and be pirates with me, or you will walk the plank tonight," said Hook.
s.fr: « Rejoignez mon équipage et soyez des pirates avec moi, ou vous marcherez sur la planche ce soir, » dit Hook.

s.t: "We will not be pirates," said John.
s.fr: « Nous ne serons pas pirates, » dit John.

s.t: "The plank for all of you, then!" said Hook.
s.fr: « La planche pour vous tous, alors ! » dit Hook.

s.t: The boys looked down at the black water, and at Wendy.
s.fr: Les garçons regardèrent en-bas vers l’eau noire, et vers Wendy.

s.t: "Do not be afraid of them," said Wendy to her boys.
s.fr: « N’ayez pas peur d’eux, » dit Wendy à ses garçons.

paras.summary: On the deck of the pirate ship the children are tied to the mast, and Hook tells them to join his crew or walk the plank tonight; John says they will not be pirates, and Wendy tells her boys not to be afraid.

s.t: From over the water came a sound: tick, tick.
s.fr: De par-dessus l’eau vint un son : tic-tac, tic-tac.

s.t: The pirates stood still on the deck.
s.fr: Les pirates restèrent immobiles sur le pont.

s.t: "The crocodile!" cried a pirate.
s.fr: « Le crocodile ! » cria un pirate.

s.t: Hook ran from the deck and hid inside the ship.
s.fr: Hook quitta le pont en courant et se cacha à l’intérieur du navire.

paras.summary: A tick, tick comes over the water, and the pirates stand still and believe the crocodile has come for their captain at last, and Hook runs and hides inside the ship.

s.t: But it was not the crocodile.
s.fr: Mais ce n’était pas le crocodile.

s.t: It was Peter, low over the water, and the sound of the clock came from his mouth.
s.fr: C’était Peter, bas sur l’eau, et le son de l’horloge venait de sa bouche.

s.t: No pirate saw the boy climb up over the side of the ship.
s.fr: Aucun pirate ne vit le garçon grimper par-dessus le bord du navire.

paras.summary: But it is not the crocodile — it is Peter, low over the water, the sound of the clock coming from his own mouth — and while the pirates look at the water, no one sees the boy climb up over the side of the ship.

s.t: Peter cut the ropes from the mast with his dagger, and the children were free.
s.fr: Peter coupa les cordes du mât avec son poignard, et les enfants étaient libres.

s.t: The boys took swords from a chest by the mast, without a sound.
s.fr: Les garçons prirent des épées dans un coffre près du mât, sans un bruit.

s.t: When the tick stopped, Hook came out and saw Peter by the mast, with the children free.
s.fr: Quand le tic-tac s’arrêta, Hook sortit et vit Peter près du mât, avec les enfants libres.

s.t: "Pan!" cried Hook.
s.fr: « Pan ! » cria Hook.

paras.summary: Peter cuts the ropes with his dagger, the boys take swords from a chest by the mast without a sound, and when the tick stops, Hook comes out and sees Peter by the mast and the children free, and cries out Pan's name.

s.t: Hook ran at Peter with his sword and his iron hook.
s.fr: Hook courut vers Peter avec son épée et son crochet de fer.

s.t: Peter jumped away, and then they fought.
s.fr: Peter sauta de côté, et ensuite ils se battirent.

s.t: The sword was long, but the dagger was fast.
s.fr: L’épée était longue, mais le poignard était rapide.

paras.summary: Hook runs at Peter with his sword, and they fight; the sword is long but the dagger is fast, and the iron hook does not come near Peter.

s.t: The lost boys ran at the pirates with swords, and John and Michael fought side by side.
s.fr: Les garçons perdus coururent vers les pirates avec des épées, et John et Michael se battirent côte à côte.

s.t: The pirates were afraid, for they had heard the tick, tick that night.
s.fr: Les pirates avaient peur, car ils avaient entendu le tic-tac, tic-tac cette nuit-là.

s.t: With a great cry, the pirates jumped into the sea and swam away for the island.
s.fr: Avec un grand cri, les pirates sautèrent dans la mer et nagèrent au loin vers l’île.

s.t: Hook stood alone with Peter, and Wendy held the boys back from the fight.
s.fr: Hook se retrouva seul avec Peter, et Wendy retint les garçons loin du combat.

paras.summary: The lost boys run at the pirates with their swords, John and Michael fighting side by side, and the pirates, still afraid from the tick that night, jump into the sea with a great cry and swim for the island, leaving Hook alone while Wendy holds the boys back.

s.t: Step by step, Hook went back to the side of the ship.
s.fr: Pas à pas, Hook recula vers le bord du navire.

s.t: From the dark water below came the tick, tick of the clock.
s.fr: Des profondeurs sombres en dessous montait le tic-tac, tic-tac de l’horloge.

s.t: Hook saw green eyes down in the black water at the side of the ship.
s.fr: Hook vit des yeux verts en bas dans l’eau noire au bord du navire.

s.t: The crocodile had come at last for the rest of him.
s.fr: Le crocodile était venu enfin pour le reste de lui.

s.t: Peter came at him fast with the dagger, and Hook fell from the side of the ship.
s.fr: Peter fonça sur lui rapidement avec le poignard, et Hook tomba du bord du navire.

s.t: The crocodile closed its jaws on Hook, and Captain Hook was gone.
s.fr: Le crocodile referma ses mâchoires sur Hook, et le Capitaine Hook avait disparu.

paras.summary: Peter and Hook fight up and down the ship, and step by step Hook goes back to the side; then the tick, tick comes from the dark water below, where green eyes wait, for the crocodile has come at last for the rest of him — Peter comes on fast, Hook falls from the side, and the crocodile closes its jaws on him, and Captain Hook is gone.

s.t: The boys took down Hook's black flag with the skull on it.
s.fr: Les garçons descendirent le drapeau noir de Hook avec le crâne dessus.

s.t: John stood at the wheel, for he had thought of pirate ships long before.
s.fr: John se tint à la barre, car il avait pensé aux navires pirates bien avant.

s.t: That night, the children slept in the pirates' beds, and Peter slept in Hook's bed.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, les enfants dormirent dans les lits des pirates, et Peter dormit dans le lit de Hook.

s.t: In the morning, they would fly home at last, over the sea.
s.fr: Le matin, ils rentreraient enfin chez eux, en volant au-dessus de la mer.

paras.summary: The fight is over and the children have won the pirate ship; the boys take down the black flag with the skull on it, John stands at the wheel he once thought of, and that night the children sleep in the pirates' beds, ready to fly home in the morning.

s.t: In the morning, the children and Peter flew up together, and they flew home over the sea.
s.fr: Le matin, les enfants et Peter s’envolèrent ensemble, et ils rentrèrent chez eux en volant au-dessus de la mer.

s.t: Peter and Tinker Bell came first, over the streets, to the tall house and the window.
s.fr: Peter et Tinker Bell arrivèrent en premier, au-dessus des rues, jusqu’à la grande maison et la fenêtre.

s.t: He wanted to close the window, for then Wendy would believe her mother had forgotten her.
s.fr: Il voulait fermer la fenêtre, car alors Wendy croirait que sa mère l’avait oubliée.

s.t: And then she would go back over the sea to Neverland, home with him.
s.fr: Et alors elle retournerait au-dessus de la mer vers Neverland, chez lui.

paras.summary: In the morning they all fly home over the sea, and Peter and Tinker Bell come first to the tall house; Peter wants to close the window so Wendy will believe her mother has forgotten her and will go back to Neverland with him.

s.t: But at the window, Peter looked in and saw the mother.
s.fr: Mais à la fenêtre, Peter regarda à l’intérieur et vit la mère.

s.t: She slept in a chair by the open window, and there were tears on her face.
s.fr: Elle dormait dans un fauteuil près de la fenêtre ouverte, et il y avait des larmes sur son visage.

s.t: Peter looked at the tears, and he could not close the window on the mother.
s.fr: Peter regarda les larmes, et il ne pouvait pas fermer la fenêtre sur la mère.

s.t: He left the window open and flew up over the roof of the tall house.
s.fr: Il laissa la fenêtre ouverte et s’envola au-dessus du toit de la grande maison.

paras.summary: But at the window Peter sees the mother asleep in a chair with tears on her face, and he cannot close the window on her; he leaves it open and flies up over the roof.

s.t: Wendy, John, and Michael flew in through the open window.
s.fr: Wendy, John, et Michael entrèrent par la fenêtre ouverte.

s.t: They went to their own beds without a sound.
s.fr: Ils allèrent dans leurs propres lits sans faire de bruit.

s.t: Their mother slept on in her chair, and the moon was on the sill.
s.fr: Leur mère continua de dormir dans son fauteuil, et la lune était sur le rebord.

s.t: The mother woke and saw the children, and she believed it was a dream she had dreamed many times.
s.fr: La mère se réveilla et vit les enfants, et elle crut que c’était un rêve qu’elle avait rêvé bien des fois.

s.t: "Mother, Mother, we are home!" called Wendy.
s.fr: « Maman, Maman, nous sommes à la maison ! » appela Wendy.

s.t: Wendy went to her mother and held her hand, and the hand was warm.
s.fr: Wendy alla vers sa mère et prit sa main, et la main était chaude.

paras.summary: The children fly in through the open window and get into their own beds without a sound while the mother sleeps on; she wakes and believes it is a dream she has dreamed many times, until Wendy calls out and holds her hand, and the hand is warm.

s.t: It was not a dream, and the mother ran to the beds and hugged all the children together.
s.fr: Ce n’était pas un rêve, et la mère courut vers les lits et serra tous les enfants ensemble.

s.t: The father came in, and the family was together again.
s.fr: Le père entra, et la famille était de nouveau réunie.

paras.summary: It is not a dream: the mother runs to the beds, hugs all the children together, and kisses them again and again; the father comes in and holds them too, the mother sings, and she cries that night, but not as she cried before.

s.t: The children had grown a little, but the mother knew every face.
s.fr: Les enfants avaient grandi un peu, mais la mère connaissait chaque visage.

s.t: The lost boys stood at the window and looked in at the family.
s.fr: Les garçons perdus se tenaient à la fenêtre et regardaient la famille à l’intérieur.

s.t: "They have no mother and no father," said Wendy.
s.fr: « Ils n’ont ni mère ni père, » dit Wendy.

s.t: "We will be their mother and father," said the mother.
s.fr: « Nous serons leur mère et leur père, » dit la mère.

s.t: The mother and father said yes to every one of the lost boys.
s.fr: La mère et le père dirent oui à chacun des garçons perdus.

s.t: The boys came in through the window, glad of a home at last.
s.fr: Les garçons entrèrent par la fenêtre, contents d’avoir enfin un foyer.

paras.summary: The children have grown a little, but the mother knows every face; the lost boys stand at the window, and when Wendy says they have no mother and no father, the mother and father say yes to every one of them, and the boys come in, glad of a home at last.

s.t: The mother asked Peter to come in too.
s.fr: La mère demanda à Peter d’entrer aussi.

s.t: "They will make me go to school and grow up," said Peter.
s.fr: « Ils me feront aller à l’école et grandir, » dit Peter.

s.t: "No one will ever make me grow up."
s.fr: « Personne ne me fera jamais grandir. »

s.t: Peter said goodbye to Wendy at the window.
s.fr: Peter dit au revoir à Wendy à la fenêtre.

s.t: He flew back to Neverland with Tinker Bell, and he stayed young.
s.fr: Il retourna en volant à Neverland avec Tinker Bell, et il resta jeune.

paras.summary: Every lost boy has a mother and a father now, with supper and a fire that night; the mother asks Peter in too, but they would make him go to school and grow up, and no one will ever make him grow up, so he says goodbye to Wendy at the window and flies back to Neverland with Tinker Bell, still young.

s.t: Sometimes, at story time, a boy came and sat outside the nursery window to listen.
s.fr: Parfois, à l’heure des histoires, un garçon venait et s’asseyait dehors à la fenêtre de la nursery pour écouter.

s.t: The mother saw him there and knew him now, and she did not close the window.
s.fr: La mère le vit là et le connut alors, et elle ne ferma pas la fenêtre.

s.t: Wendy told the stories again, and the boy at the window listened.
s.fr: Wendy raconta les histoires de nouveau, et le garçon à la fenêtre écouta.

s.t: The lost boys listened too, for the stories were their stories now.
s.fr: Les garçons perdus écoutèrent aussi, car les histoires étaient leurs histoires maintenant.

s.t: The best stories were still about Peter Pan.
s.fr: Les meilleures histoires parlaient encore de Peter Pan.

paras.summary: Sometimes, at story time, a boy comes and sits outside the nursery window to listen; the mother knows him now and does not close the window, Wendy tells the stories again, the lost boys listen too, and the best stories are still about Peter Pan — who stays young forever, as the stories say — and the window stays open for him always.
